newsitem.title: FRANCE: Summer tourists take to skis in southern France.
newsitem.headline: Summer tourists take to skis in southern France.

text.p: Tourists who had expected to sunbathe in southwest France's Pyrenees at the start of their summer holiday took to their skis instead on Sunday.
Some 80 hikers were stranded in mountain refuges as snow fell above 1,300 metres (4,300 ft), the first time in three decades residents saw snow at such a low altitude in late June.
Holidaymakers skied down the road from the 2,100-metre-high (6,900 ft) Tourmalet pass which was under 20 cm (eight inches) of snow and closed to traffic.

In one of the wettest months of June on record, showers kept falling on most of the country and the weather institute forecast more snow on Monday on the Alps and Pyrenees mountains -- but only above 2,000 metres (6,600 ft).
